The 2025 BMW X7 xDrive40i is the entry-level trim of BMW's largest luxury SUV, blending high-tech refinement with a versatile three-row cabin. It starts at an MSRP of approximately $84,300.
Performance & Powertrain
Engine: 3.0L BMW Twin Power Turbo inline 6-cylinder engine with a 48V mild hybrid system.
Output: 375 horsepower and 398 lb-ft of torque.
Acceleration: 060 mph in 5.2 to 5.6 seconds.
Fuel Economy: EPA-estimated 20 city/24 highway/22 combined MPG.
Drivetrain: Standard xDrive Intelligent All-Wheel Drive and an 8-speed Sport Automatic transmission.
Key Features & Interior
Seating: Standard for 7 passengers, optional second-row captain's chairs reduce capacity to 6 but improve third-row access.
Tech: Features the BMW Curved Display with a 12.3" digital cluster and 14.9" touchscreen running iDrive 8.5.
Standard Luxuries: Multi-color ambient lighting, heated front seats/armrests/steering wheel, and a panoramic moonroof.
Cargo Space: Offers up to 90.4 cubic feet with the rear seats folded.

You can also tame twisty roads with the sport-tuned suspension while you reach nearly 22mpg on the highway in this Rear Wheel Drive SUV. Our Durango takes an athletic stance with the Blacktop Package's 20-inch high-gloss black aluminum wheels, gloss black badges, and gloss black mirrors matched by LED lighting and a performance hood with center air intakes and dual heat extractors. The R/T then brings upscale athletic details into its seven-place cabin. Safety and Security
  • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.
  • Rear camera - Watching your back! The rear camera helps you see obstacles and hazards you otherwise couldn't by showing enhanced images of what is behind you. The rear camera is an extra set of eyes that's both convenient and safe.
  • Lane departure prevention - Keep it between the lines. It only takes a moment of inattention for your vehicle to drift. With lane departure prevention, your vehicle takes corrective action to help you avoid unintentionally moving out of your lane. Lane departure prevention is an extra level of safety for you and those around you.
  • Head-up display - Keep your head up! You don't have to take your eyes off of the road to get information from your dashboard anymore. With head-up display, important driving information - like speed and RPM's - displays on your windshield in your line of sight. Because when you're driving, the most important information lies on the road ahead. Keep your eyes on the road with head-up display.
Technology and Telematics
  • Smart device mirroring - Smartphone, meet smart car. You can control your device through your vehicle's infotainment system. Smart device mirroring brings together safety and convenience by making it easier to find what you're looking for while keeping your eyes on the road.
  • Mobile hotspot - WiFi on the fly. Connect your devices to the Internet through your vehicle's private mobile hotspot and take the internet wherever your journey takes you, without eating up your data allowance. Find the hotspot with mobile hotspot.

Its nine-speed transmission offers the ultimate balance between fuel efficiency and performance. It saves gasoline while ensuring the smoothest operation. The BMW M5 stands as the ultimate evolution of the performance sedan––delivering electrified speed, comfort, and refinement that rival exotic supercars, yet remains as comfortable and usable as any BMW daily driver. Theres a kind of cinematic vertigo to the 2021 Model S Plaid an electric grand tourer that reads like minimalism gone feral. At rest its deceptively composed: a clean, aerodynamic silhouette that favors purpose over ornament, glass that flows uninterrupted, and surfaces that catch light with a cool, deliberate clarity. Up close, the details reveal impatience: muscular haunches, a low posture, and a presence that suggests the car is practicing restraint only until you ask otherwise. It looks like a luxury saloon thats spent the afternoon at the gym polished, disciplined and ready for mischief.

Slide inside and the cabin is both spaceship and salon. Materials are chosen for their tactile honesty: smooth leather, cool metals and a pared-back dashboard that refuses to overdecorate. The minimalist aesthetic amplifies the sensation of space, a wide floor and expansive glass create an airy stage while the driver-centric layout keeps the senses engaged. Seats wrap with an athletic courtesy, supportive enough to invite commitment yet comfortable for long stretches. Small details the weight of a switch, the angle of a seam, a well-placed cupholder remind you the experience was curated, not assembled by committee.

On the road the Plaid is theatrical in a matter-of-fact way. Acceleration is not merely brisk, its an almost absurd translation of intent into momentum, immediate and relentless. The sensation is clean and scientific: a linear shove that unspools without drama but leaves you recalibrating what quick means. Steering is precise and communicative, the chassis crisp and unflappable, so high speeds feel less like danger and more like deft translation of composure into velocity. The car rewards decisive inputs and punishes hesitation it wants to be driven with confidence.

Sound design is integral: lacking a traditional engines roar, it composes its own soundtrack of electric whine and purposeful mechanical notes that feel engineered to thrill rather than startle. Tech lives like a discreet companion large displays and clever interfaces that serve the drive while keeping clutter at bay. Practical comforts are thoughtfully integrated: cargo that actually works, cabin quiet that preserves conversation, and an interior tuned for daily life as much as spectacle.

In short, the 2021 Model S Plaid is a study in focused contradiction serene in design, unhinged in propulsion, luxurious in restraint and thrilling when provoked. Its a modern performance statement: surgical, civilized and impossible to ignore.

  • GPS linked cruise control - Set it and forget it. Road trips used to be stressful, until GPS linked cruise control set the pace. Safety and Security
  • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.

This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.

Technology and Telematics

In cases where a customer is dissatisfied with a vehicle they have purchased new from a manufacturer, they may offer or agree to reacquire the vehicle and give the customer a refund or a replacement vehicle. In many cases, the manufacturer is unable to verify the concern, but agrees to take the vehicle back in the interest of customer satisfaction. In other cases, a required part or software update may not be available. Buybacks always carry the remaining balance of the factory warranty. In some cases, an extended warranty on the repaired defect also applies. Auto manufacturers value their reputation. That reputation is an integral part of the value attached to the models that they sell. Vehicles repurchased by a manufacturer may need repairs to correct problems, but that isn't always the case. Vehicles are often repurchased as a gesture of goodwill to maintain a valued relationship with a customer. In other instances, parts may not have been available in a timely manner to fix a minor problem and the customer may ask the manufacturer buy back the vehicle. There are even cases where buyers will fabricate problems to get out of a vehicle if they know how to use the "Lemon Laws" to their advantage. Furthermore, there are situations where a vehicle does have a legitimate mechanical problem that needs extra attention to correct. Regardless of the reason for a buyback, when a true problem does exist, the manufacturer not only wants to fix it, the company is required by law to fully correct any issues before the vehicle is offered for sale.
